'Deleting the last section or the selected field, long names, live preview
'No
'Long names are now cut with '…' and show the full name when you hover over them.

'The spec line is the same in both versions: 'A very long field or section name is shortened in the canvas, the outline and the properties panel rather than breaking the layout.' The later decision is the designer's, on 12 Oct: 'Let's truncate text with "…" and show tooltip on hover which displays full text', built on 12-13 Oct ('Builder: field rows, section heading and outline names end with "…" with the full name on hover'). Hovering over a shortened name: before, nothing was required; now a tooltip shows the full name. Neither the 22 Sep spec nor the 22 Sep design has a full-name tooltip.
'SV-11103: 12 Oct 2026 (Branko Cicovic (designer) in Jira)
'A very long field or section name is shortened in the canvas, the outline and the properties panel rather than breaking the layout.

'A very long field or section name is shortened with '…' on the canvas and in the outline, without breaking the layout (unchanged).
Hovering over a shortened name - a field row or section heading on the canvas, or a name in the outline - shows the full name in a tooltip.
'3. Confirm a very long field or section name is shortened in the canvas, the outline and the properties panel rather than breaking the layout.

'1. Give a field and a section very long names.
2. Check each is shortened with '…' on the canvas and in the outline.
3. Hover over the shortened field name on the canvas.
4. Check a tooltip shows the full name.
5. Hover over the shortened section heading on the canvas.
6. Check a tooltip shows the full name.
7. Hover over the shortened name in the outline.
8. Check a tooltip shows the full name.

'Designer-only source: the tooltip was decided by the designer on 12 Oct and built on 12-13 Oct. The 14 Oct spec still says only 'shortened', and no product manager sign-off is recorded (he was only copied). It adds to the old expectation rather than contradicting it; consider asking the product owner to confirm it. The decision does not mention the properties panel, so no tooltip is expected there.

'What the customer report says, and what it no longer shows
'Yes
'The report now prints each axle as one block with the axle's result in its header and no per-row status column, with icons as well as colour.

'Before (22 Sep spec): 'A per-axle field will print each row's values per position, with a status column carrying the row's derived verdict.' Now (14 Oct spec): 'A per-axle field will print one block per axle, never split across a page: each row's values per position, and the axle's result in the axle header. The sub-tables are headed by scope, 'OUTER + INNER' and '1 PER SIDE'. A flagged value carries ... a triangle for Needs attention and a clock for Monitor, as well as its colour ... A position nobody measured prints a grey dash. There is no per-row status column.' The report now has no status column, shows the result in each axle header, and adds the icons, the scope headings and the grey dash.
'S13-R0: 5 Oct 2026 (Developer and QA questions answered)
'A per-axle field prints each row's values per position, with a status column carrying the row's derived verdict.

'A per-axle field prints one block per axle, never split across a page.
Each block shows each row's values per position, and the axle's result in the axle header, in the report's words: ATTENTION, MONITOR or PASS (this wording itself is unchanged; the report already never printed Not OK).
There is no status column per row.
The sub-tables are headed 'OUTER + INNER' and '1 PER SIDE'.
A flagged value carries an icon as well as its colour: a triangle for Needs attention, a clock for Monitor.
A position nobody measured prints a grey dash.
'1. Confirm a per-axle field prints each row's values per position with a status column carrying the row's derived verdict.

'1. Make sure the per-axle field has a tire row on 'Outer + inner', a row on '1 per side', Monitor and Not OK values, at least one empty position, and enough axles that the field runs past the first page of the report (for example 8).
2. Open the inspection's report.
3. Check each axle prints as one block that is not split across pages.
4. Check each axle header shows the axle's result as ATTENTION, MONITOR or PASS (unchanged wording), and there is no status column per row.
5. Check the sub-tables are headed 'OUTER + INNER' and '1 PER SIDE'.
6. Check each flagged value has a triangle (Needs attention) or a clock (Monitor) as well as its colour.
7. Check the empty position prints a grey dash.

'The change is the layout: one block per axle with the axle's result in its header, no per-row status column, icons as well as colour, and a grey dash for unmeasured positions (decided 5 Oct). The result words ATTENTION, MONITOR and PASS are not new. The 22 Sep design brief also planned a per-row status column, so the old expectation was consistent across sources.

'The customer report stays correct when regenerated or republished
'No
'Regenerating a report must now keep the first-completion inspected date and must not post another note on the work order.

'The 22 Sep spec only said 'The inspected date will show without a time' and said nothing about notes when a report is regenerated. Now (14 Oct spec): 'The inspected date is the date the inspection was first completed. Regenerating a report does not move it' and 'Regenerating a report does not post another note on the work order.' After a regenerate the tester must now find the same number of report notes and the same inspected date.

'S13-R14: 5 Oct 2026 (Developer and QA questions answered)
S13-R15: 5 Oct 2026 (Developer and QA questions answered)

'Regenerating a report produces a new version rather than replacing the previous one, every link resolves to the most recent, and earlier versions remain retrievable so a report already handed to a customer cannot change.

'Regenerating a report does not post another note on the work order.
Regenerating does not change the inspected date: it stays the date the inspection was first completed.

'1. Regenerate the report and confirm a new version is produced rather than replacing the previous one, every link resolves to the most recent, and earlier versions remain retrievable so a report already handed to a customer cannot change.

'1. Open a completed inspection that was first completed on an earlier day (for example yesterday) and has not been reopened since.
2. Note the inspected date on its report.
3. Count the inspection report notes on the work order's Notes tab.
4. Regenerate the report.
5. Check no new note was added to the Notes tab.
6. Open the report (View PDF) and check it shows the same inspected date as before.

'Added requirement - the 22 Sep spec was silent on both points, so these are new requirements, not reversed ones. Decided by the product manager on 5 Oct in answer to questions raised during the build. Nothing shows whether the product already behaved this way. A new version being produced, every link opening the newest version, the existing note pointing at the newest version and earlier versions staying retrievable are unchanged and are left out.

'On a phone: reference files, outstanding work and the back button
'No
'Selecting an outstanding item now goes to that item's field, and a separate 'Go to the first one' action goes to the first.

'Before (22 Sep spec): 'Selecting an outstanding item will move to the first field that still needs an answer, rather than to a summary of what is missing.' Now (14 Oct spec): 'Selecting an outstanding item will move to that field. A 'Go to the first one' action moves to the first item in the list.' Selecting the third item: before, the tester landed on the first unanswered field; now on that item's own field, and a 'Go to the first one' action appears.
'S14-R7: between 29 Sep 2026 and 13 Oct 2026 (not in the change log)
'Selecting an outstanding item moves to the first field that still needs an answer, rather than to a summary of what is missing.

'Selecting an outstanding item moves to that item's own field, not to the first unanswered field.
A 'Go to the first one' action moves to the first item in the list.
'3. Select an outstanding item and confirm it moves to the first field that still needs an answer, not to a summary of what is missing.

'1. On the phone, leave at least three required fields unanswered, in different sections.
2. Press 'Submit & Generate Report' to open the list of outstanding items.
3. Select the third item in the list.
4. Check the screen moves to that item's field.
5. Open the list again and press 'Go to the first one'.
6. Check the screen moves to the first item in the list.

'Not in the change log. The 22 Sep follow-up design already showed selecting a row going to that field and a 'Go to the first one' action, but the 22 Sep spec and user story said the first unfilled field, and the case followed the spec.
